quote: Counterexample 3.2 Let Xi ∼ LL(σi, λi) and Yi ∼ (σi, δi), i = 1, 2, 3. Let (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (0.1, 0.3, 4.1) ∈ E+ and (δ1, δ2, δ3) = (0.2, 0.3, 4) ∈ E+, giving λ ≽^m δ. Now, if (σ1, σ2, σ3) = (0.1, 3, 5) ∈ E+ is taken, then Figure 2(a) shows that F3:3(x)/G3:3(x) is increasing in x. Again if (σ1, σ2, σ3) = (2, 3, 5) ∈ E+ is taken, then Figure 2(b) shows that F3:3(x)/G3:3(x) is decreasing in x. So, it can be concluded that, for all σ, λ, δ ∈ D+ (resp. E+), λ ≽^m δ does not always imply X3:3 ≤rhr Y3:3.
